Exact fractions

Source: R/fraction.R
fraction.Rd

A fraction vector stores the numerator and denominator of each element separately, as whole numbers. Fractions are kept as they were written, so fraction(2, 4) is 2/4, while results of calculations are exact and in lowest terms.

new_fraction() is a low-level constructor for developers. It requires n and d to be of the same type (integer or double) and size, with non-negative d, and doesn't check their values.

Usage

fraction(n = integer(), d = 1L)

new_fraction(n = integer(), d = integer())

is_fraction(x)

Arguments

n, d

For fraction() and new_fraction(), the numerator and denominator as whole numbers. fraction() recycles inputs of size 1. If either is missing, the fraction is missing.

x

An object to test.

Value

fraction() and new_fraction() return a fraction vector. is_fraction() returns TRUE or FALSE.

Details

The numerator and denominator are either both integers, or both doubles if either input is a double. Integers use half the memory, and become doubles if a result needs larger numbers. Doubles are limited to whole numbers up to 2^53 (about 9e15).

The sign is stored in the numerator. A denominator of zero gives 1/0, -1/0 and 0/0, which behave as Inf, -Inf and NaN. Names and dimensions are not supported; they are dropped and an error respectively.

See also

fraction-arithmetic, fraction-comparison, as_fraction(), numerator()

Examples

fraction(1, 3) + fraction(1, 6)
#> <fraction<double>[1]>
#> [1] 1/2

# The fraction is kept as written
x <- fraction(c(2, 30), c(4, 100))
x
#> <fraction<double>[2]>
#> [1]    2/4 30/100
simplify(x)
#> <fraction<double>[2]>
#> [1]  1/2 3/10

# Stored as integers
fraction(1:3, 4L)
#> <fraction<integer>[3]>
#> [1] 1/4 2/4 3/4
